subject.title: Feature: browser tool - expose CDP Network domain for request interception

question: Should OpenClaw expose browser network data to model-facing browser-tool calls, and should the first supported contract be passive redacted diagnostics or active request interception/mutation?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent contract controls sensitive authenticated browser traffic and cannot be safely chosen by automation.

options.title: Ship passive redacted diagnostics first
options.body: Expose request listing and bounded response-body retrieval through the browser tool with redaction, profile support, output wrapping, and focused tests before considering active interception.

options.title: Allow active interception with explicit policy
options.body: Add request interception or mutation only after maintainers define permissions, opt-in behavior, profile limits, and security review requirements.

options.title: Keep network inspection off model tools
options.body: Leave network inspection on CLI/control/API or external workflows if model-facing access is judged too risky.

recommendation.title: Ship passive redacted diagnostics first
recommendation.body: Expose request listing and bounded response-body retrieval through the browser tool with redaction, profile support, output wrapping, and focused tests before considering active interception.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest current history on the browser plugin schema, runtime ownership split, and model-facing browser tool surface.
